altitude.description: This field gives the altitude at which the flight can do this operation, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the flight does this operation.

description.description: This field gives the data about this operation and its local conditions, as free text.

id.description: This field identifies this flight operation. Other records and orders use it to refer to this flight operation.

instructions.description: This list contains the instructions for this flight operation.

kind.description: This field gives the type of flight operation, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.hold: The flight holds at a point or in an area.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies an operation that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.recovery: The flight goes back to an airfield for the landing.
x-enum-descriptions.refuel: This value identifies air-to-air refuelling from a flight that helps.
x-enum-descriptions.station: This value identifies time on station in an area.
x-enum-descriptions.task: This value identifies the execution of the tasking of the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.transit: This value identifies a flight from one point to a different point.

support_flight.description: This field identifies the flight that helps with this operation, such as the tanker for a refuelling operation.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the flight does this operation.

at.description: This field gives the time before which the event does not occur. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a time condition not before a time.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls the mission.

check_in.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flights follow when they first contact the agency.

handovers.description: This list identifies the command and control agencies that get the control of the mission after the first agency. The list is in the sequence of the handovers.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as control by an agency.

AirAssaultBrief.description: An air assault brief is the data that air assault aircrews get before the mission. FM 3-99 (2015) Chapters 12 and 13 give the air movement table and the lifts, serials and chalks.

air_movement_table.description: This list contains the lines of the air movement table, in order.

corridors.description: This list identifies the air corridors and transit routes that are for the serials.

escort_missions.description: This list identifies the escort and attack missions that defend the serials.

h_hour.description: This field gives the time at which the first serial is on the landing zone (LZ).

landing_zones.description: This list identifies the landing zones (LZs) that the troops go out of the aircraft at.

pickup_zones.description: This list identifies the pickup zones (PZs) that the troops go into the aircraft at.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

routes.description: This list identifies the routes that the serials fly between the pickup zones (PZs) and the landing zones (LZs).

AirMovementLine.description: An air movement line is one line of the air movement table, for one serial of one lift. FM 3-99 (2015) paragraph 12-37 gives the data of the line.

chalks.description: This list contains the chalk numbers of the aircraft in the serial.

flight.description: This field identifies the flight that flies the serial.

landing_formation.description: This field gives the formation of the serial when it lands, as one of the enumerated values.

landing_heading.description: This field gives the heading of the serial when it lands, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

landing_time.description: This field gives the time at which the serial is on the landing zone (LZ).

landing_zone.description: This field identifies the landing zone (LZ) that is the end of the flight of the serial.

lift.description: This field gives the number of the lift of the line.

lifted_unit.description: This field gives the name of the unit in the serial, as free text.

line.description: This field gives the number of the line in the air movement table.

load.description: This field gives the personnel and the cargo of the serial.

load_time.description: This field gives the time at which the troops go into the aircraft at the pickup zone (PZ).

pickup_zone.description: This field identifies the pickup zone (PZ) that the serial loads at.

release_point.description: This field identifies the release point that the serial flies through before the landing zone (LZ).

release_point_time.description: This field gives the time at which the serial is at the release point.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes about this serial, such as a change of time, as free text.

route.description: This field identifies the route that is for the serial.

serial.description: This field gives the number of the serial in the lift.

start_point.description: This field identifies the start point that the serial flies through after the pickup zone (PZ).

start_point_time.description: This field gives the time at which the serial is at the start point.

takeoff_time.description: This field gives the time of of the departure of the serial from the pickup zone (PZ).

AirToAirBrief.description: An air-to-air brief is the data for a combat air patrol (CAP), a fighter sweep, an air intercept or an escort.

bullseye.description: This field identifies the bullseye that is the reference point of the controller and the fighters. The point shall have the role `bullseye`.

commit_criteria.description: This list contains the commit criteria that start an engagement of an air track.

controller.description: This field gives the agency that controls the fighters, such as an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS), with its radio channels.

identification_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the identification matrix and the rules of engagement (ROE) for air tracks.

protected_measures.description: This list identifies the orbits and areas that the fighters defend, such as tanker and Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) orbits.

protected_missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the fighters defend.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

roe_reference.description: This field identifies the part of the special instructions (SPINS) or of a different document that gives the rules of engagement (ROE).

threat_emitters.description: This list identifies the surface-to-air emitters that the fighters avoid.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the airborne control task.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of this airborne control task, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the airborne control station is.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this airborne control task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

control_responsibilities.description: This list contains the control and surveillance tasks of the airborne control mission.

datalink.description: This field gives the data link and identification values of the airborne control task.

handover.description: This field gives the instructions for the handover of the airborne control station, as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an airborne control tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the airborne control task is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the airborne control task sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

station_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the airborne control aircraft are on station.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the airborne control task, as free text.

supported_missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the airborne control task helps.

AirborneControlBrief.description: An airborne control brief is the data that an airborne control aircrew gets before the mission.

bullseye.description: This field identifies the bullseye that is the reference point of the controllers. The point shall have the role `bullseye`.

controlled_channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that the control aircraft uses to control flights.

handover_points.description: This list identifies the points that flights change controller at. Each point shall have the role `handover` or `control`.

orbit.description: This field identifies the orbit or airborne early warning area that is the station of the control aircraft.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

sectors.description: This list contains the control sectors of the control aircraft.

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude that the order gives for the airborne launch, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

at.description: This field gives the time at which the flight starts in the air. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an airborne start.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the airborne launch, as latitude and longitude.

speed.description: This field gives the speed of the flight at the start in the air, as a speed with its unit.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

fuel.description: This field gives the fuel plan of this aircraft, which replaces the fuel plan of the flight.

identification.description: This field gives the identification values of this aircraft, which replace the values of the flight.

member.description: This field gives the position number of this aircraft in the flight, from 1.

scl.description: This field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that this aircraft has, which replaces the primary SCL of the flight.

AirdropBrief.description: An airdrop brief is the data for an airdrop mission. FM 3-99 (2015) Chapter 5 and FM 3-21.38 (2006) Chapter 6 give these data.

authentication_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the authentication between the aircrew and the drop zone (DZ) support team.

clear_to_drop_signal.description: This field gives the signal that gives the clearance to release the load, as one of the enumerated values.

code_letter.description: This field gives the code letter on the drop zone (DZ), as one letter from `A` to `Z`.

drop_airspeed.description: This field gives the airspeed at which the aircraft release the load, with its unit.

drop_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude at which the aircraft release the load, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

drop_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the aircraft release the load.

drop_zone.description: This field identifies the drop zone (DZ) that receives the airdrop.

drop_zone_controller.description: This field gives the agency that controls the drop zone (DZ), with its radio channels.

load_type.description: This field gives the type of the load, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.container_delivery_system: This value identifies an airdrop of supplies in containers. The containers go out of the rear of the aircraft in sequence, because of their weight.
x-enum-descriptions.door_bundle: This value identifies a small load that the aircrew pushes out of a door at the side of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.heavy_equipment: This value identifies a heavy drop of vehicles or equipment on platforms.
x-enum-descriptions.personnel: This value identifies a drop of troops or other personnel with parachutes.
x-enum-descriptions.precision_airdrop: This value identifies an airdrop in which a guidance system moves the parachute of each load to the point of impact.

markings.description: This list contains the markings of the drop zone (DZ) that the aircrew looks for.

x-enum-descriptions.code_letter: This value identifies a large letter on the ground at the drop zone (DZ). The aircrew compares it with the code letter of the brief to make sure that the DZ is correct.
x-enum-descriptions.lights: This value identifies marker lights on the ground that show the drop zone (DZ) to the aircrew, usually at night.
x-enum-descriptions.panels: This value identifies panels with bright colours on the ground that show the drop zone (DZ) to the aircrew.
x-enum-descriptions.raised_angle_marker: This value identifies a raised angle marker at the point of impact.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies smoke on the ground that shows the drop zone (DZ) and the wind direction to the aircrew.

parachute_technique.description: This field gives the parachute method of the personnel drop, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.haho: This value identifies a high-altitude high-opening (HAHO) personnel drop. The personnel open their parachutes at high altitude a short time after they go out of the aircraft. Then they fly a long distance to the drop zone (DZ) with their parachutes.
x-enum-descriptions.halo: This value identifies a high-altitude low-opening (HALO) personnel drop. The personnel go out of the aircraft at high altitude and open their parachutes at low altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.static_line: This value identifies a parachute drop at low altitude. A line in the aircraft opens each parachute when the person goes out of the aircraft.

point_of_impact.description: This field identifies the point that is the point of impact on the drop zone (DZ).

release_method.description: This field gives the method that sets the release point, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.carp: This value identifies a computed air release point (CARP) that the aircrew calculates.
x-enum-descriptions.gmrs: This value identifies a ground-marked release system (GMRS), in which markings on the ground show the release point.
x-enum-descriptions.harp: This value identifies a high-altitude release point (HARP) for a high-altitude low-opening (HALO) or high-altitude high-opening (HAHO) personnel drop.
x-enum-descriptions.virs: This value identifies a verbally initiated release system (VIRS), in which the drop zone (DZ) support team tells the aircrew when to release.

release_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the release point in the plan.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

run_in_heading.description: This field gives the heading of the aircraft on the run-in to the drop zone (DZ), as a bearing with its unit and reference.

availability.description: This field gives the time interval during which the alert launch is available.

departure.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that keeps the alert aircraft.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an alert launch.

readiness_minutes.description: This field gives the time from the launch order until the aircraft are in the air, in minutes.

release_authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives the order to launch the alert aircraft.

Altitude.description: An altitude is a vertical position with its unit and its reference: mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

AltitudeBlock.description: An altitude block is a vertical band between a floor and a ceiling. The floor can be the surface, and the ceiling can have no limit.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area that this selection contains.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a selected area target.

target.description: This field identifies the area target that this selection contains.

at.description: This field gives the time at which the event occurs. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a time condition at a time.

tolerance_seconds.description: This field gives the maximum time interval between the event and the time in `at`, in seconds. The limit is applicable before and after that time.

activation_condition.description: This field gives the condition in which this attack assignment starts, as free text.

assigned_to.description: This list contains the flights and aircraft that attack the target.

desired_effect.description: This field gives the effect on the target that the attack assignment gives, as one of the enumerated values. The values are openAIX values with no doctrinal source.

x-enum-descriptions.DEGRADE: The attack degrades the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.DENY: After the attack, the enemy cannot use the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.DESTROY: The attack destroys the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.DISRUPT: The attack disrupts the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.DIVERT: The attack diverts the target or its resources. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.NEUTRALIZE: The attack neutralizes the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.SUPPRESS: The attack suppresses the target. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.

id.description: This field identifies this attack assignment. Other records and orders use it to refer to this attack assignment.

instructions.description: This list contains the instructions for this attack assignment.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of this attack assignment in the tasking. Priority 1 is the highest.

required_stores.description: This list identifies the stores that are necessary for the attack on the target.

restrictions.description: This list contains the limits and conditions that are applicable to this attack assignment.

role.description: This field gives the role of this attack assignment: `primary` or `alternate`, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.alternate: The selected aircraft do this assignment when the primary assignment is not possible.
x-enum-descriptions.primary: The selected aircraft do this assignment first.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the attack assignment, as free text.

target.description: This field gives the target of this attack assignment. The target is a fixed target with aimpoint identifiers, a mobile target or an area target.

target_list_entry.description: This field gives the joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL) or time-sensitive target (TST) entry of the target of this attack assignment.

timing.description: This field gives the time condition for the attack. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

weaponeering.description: This list contains the weapon loads of the flights for this attack assignment.

AttackBrief.description: An attack brief is the data that aircrews get before a preplanned attack. The role of the tasking gives the type of attack. The attack assignments of the tasking give the targets, the effects, the times on target and the weapons.

bda.description: This field gives the battle damage assessment (BDA) that the aircrews collect after the attack.

cas.description: This field gives the close air support (CAS) data. The field is applicable to the `scheduled_cas` role.

egress_points.description: This list identifies the egress points or gates that the flights fly through after the attack. Each point shall have the role `egress` or `gate`.

egress_route.description: This field identifies the route that the flights use after the attack.

ingress_route.description: This field identifies the route that the flights use to fly to the target area.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

restricted_areas.description: This list identifies the no-fire areas, restrictive fire areas or no-fly zones that are applicable to the attack. Each no-strike site near a target has a no-fire area around it.

sead.description: This field gives the suppression of enemy air defences (SEAD) data. The field is applicable to SEAD and destruction of enemy air defences (DEAD) roles.

threat_emitters.description: This list identifies the emitters that can engage the flights on the route or at the target.

BDARequirement.description: A battle damage assessment (BDA) requirement is the BDA that the aircrew collects after the attack.

deadline.description: This field gives the time before which the aircrew sends the battle damage assessment (BDA).

method.description: This field gives the method that the aircrew uses to collect the battle damage assessment (BDA), as one of the enumerated values.

recipient.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the battle damage assessment (BDA).

report.description: This field identifies the report definition that the aircrew uses to send the battle damage assessment (BDA).

at.description: This field gives the time after which the event does not occur. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a time condition not after a time.

CASBrief.description: A close air support (CAS) brief is the data that CAS aircrews get before an on-call or scheduled CAS mission. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Chapter V gives the check-in briefing and the CAS brief.

check_in.description: This field gives the check-in data for the controller.

contact_points.description: This list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role `control`.

controllers.description: This list contains the agencies that control the close air support (CAS) for this CAS mission, with their radio channels.

fire_support_measures.description: This list identifies the fire support coordination measures and airspace coordination areas that are applicable to the close air support (CAS) mission.

friendly_lines.description: This list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.

ground_scheme_summary.description: This field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.

holding_altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the close air support (CAS) mission. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this close air support (CAS) mission.

marks.description: This list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.

x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies a mark from artillery, mortar or naval gun fire.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_pointer: This value identifies a mark from an infrared pointer. Aircrew with night vision devices can see it on the target.
x-enum-descriptions.laser: This value identifies a mark from a laser target designator.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies a mark from smoke ammunition at or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.talk_on: This value identifies a talk-on, in which the controller tells the aircrew how to find the target by voice.
x-enum-descriptions.tracer: This value identifies a mark from tracer ammunition.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

handling.description: This field gives the handling instructions for this cargo item, as free text.

name.description: This field gives the name of this cargo item, for display.

quantity.description: This field gives the number of units of this cargo item.

CheckIn.description: A close air support (CAS) check-in is the data that the CAS aircrew gives to the controller at check-in. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Figure V-4 gives the check-in briefing.

abort_code.description: This field gives the abort code for the controller and the aircrew, as free text.

items.description: This list contains the parts of the check-in briefing that the aircrew gives.

x-enum-descriptions.abort_code: This value identifies the code that the aircrew uses to make sure that an abort call comes from the controller.
x-enum-descriptions.aircraft_number_and_type: This value identifies the quantity of aircraft in the flight and their aircraft type.
x-enum-descriptions.capabilities: This value identifies the sensors and the other capabilities of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.mission_number: This value identifies the mission number of the flight in the air tasking order (ATO).
x-enum-descriptions.ordnance: This value identifies the weapons on the aircraft, with the quantity of each.
x-enum-descriptions.position_and_altitude: This value identifies the position of the flight at this time, usually from a control point, and its altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.time_on_station: This value identifies the time that the aircraft can stay on station.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the check-in steps.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the flight collects the information.

collection_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the flight collects the information.

eeis.description: This list contains the essential elements of information (EEIs) of this collection.

id.description: This field identifies this essential element of information (EEI). Each EEI in its collection entry has a different identifier.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of the essential element of information (EEI). Priority 1 is the highest.

question.description: This field gives the text of the essential element of information (EEI), as free text.

id.description: This field identifies this collection entry. Other records and orders use it to refer to this collection entry.

information_required.description: This field gives the information that the flight gets, as free text.

latest_useful_time.description: This field gives the time after which the information has no value. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

product.description: This field gives the output that the flight sends, as one of the enumerated values.

recipient.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the output.

reporting.description: This field gives the method and the time of the reports for this collection.

sensor.description: This field gives the type of sensor that the flight uses for the collection, as one of the enumerated values.

target.description: This field identifies the target that the collection is about.

CommitCriterion.description: A commit criterion is a condition in which the fighters start an engagement of an air track. A commit criterion shall give a range, a boundary or a procedure.

boundary.description: This field identifies the control measure that is the boundary of this commit criterion.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the full commit criteria.

range.description: This field gives the range from the fighters or from their defended asset at which they start the engagement, as a length with its unit.

threat.description: This field identifies the threat that this commit criterion is for.

alternatives.description: This list contains the standard conventional loads (SCLs) that the flight can use as alternatives, and the conditions in which it uses them.

member_overrides.description: This list contains the values for one aircraft that are different from the values of the flight.

primary_scl.description: This field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that all aircraft of the flight have, unless an aircraft entry gives a different load.

secondary_purpose.description: This field gives the function of the standard conventional load (SCL) in `secondary_scl`, as free text.

secondary_scl.description: This field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that the flight has for a second function.

action.description: This field gives the step that the flight does when the condition occurs, as free text.

alternate_route.description: This field identifies the route that the flight uses for this contingency.

condition.description: This field gives the condition that starts this contingency, as free text.

decision_authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that makes the decision for this contingency.

divert.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that the flight goes to for this contingency.

ControlSector.description: A control sector is a part of the airspace that one controller of the control aircraft controls.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the control sector, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure that is the sector.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that is for the controller of the sector.

flights.description: This list identifies the flights that the controller of the sector controls.

missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the controller of the sector controls.

name.description: This field gives the name of this control sector, for display.

ControllerContact.description: An agency channel is an agency for the aircrew, with its radio channels.

agency.description: This field identifies the agency or forward air controller that the aircrew speaks to. The value is the identifier of a command and control agency or of a forward air controller (FAC) of the resource catalogue.

alternate_channel.description: This field identifies the alternative radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency when the primary channel is not available.

channel.description: This field identifies the primary radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency.

CounterAir.description: A counterair task is a fighter sweep or an air intercept. A fighter sweep shall have an operating area. An air intercept shall identify a target, or the area where the fighters contact the target. Combat air patrol (CAP) is a different type of tasking.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the fighters stop the task.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the counterair task, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the area or airspace that contains the fighter sweep or the air intercept.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this counterair task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

engagement_instructions.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the commit criteria and the engagement conditions.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a counterair tasking.

mission_type.description: This field gives the type of counterair task: `fighter_sweep` or `interception`, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.fighter_sweep: This value identifies an offensive counterair mission. Fighters go into a specified area to find and destroy enemy aircraft or a target of opportunity.
x-enum-descriptions.interception: This value identifies an air intercept. Fighters contact an air track to identify it. The track is a hostile track, a possibly hostile track or an unknown track. An air intercept does not authorize an engagement.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the counterair task is for, as free text.

operating_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the fighter sweep or the air intercept occurs, as the plan gives it.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the reports that the task sends.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the task, as free text.

target.description: This field identifies the mobile target that is the aircraft or the formation for the air intercept. The target is not always an enemy. Its position and simulator bindings stay on the target record.

CounterAir.title: Counterair task

CounterlandControl.description: A counterland control task is a strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR) or airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) task in a specified area. In a SCAR mission, the aircraft find targets and coordinate the attacks of other flights on them. In a FAC(A) mission, the aircraft give terminal attack control to close air support (CAS) aircraft. SCAR aircraft do not have the authority of terminal attack control.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the counterland control task.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the counterland control task, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the aircraft find targets and control the attacks.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this counterland control task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a counterland control tasking.

mission_type.description: This field gives the type of counterland control task: `scar` or `fac_a`, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.fac_a: This value identifies an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission. A FAC(A) gives terminal attack control to close air support (CAS) aircraft from the air.
x-enum-descriptions.scar: This value identifies strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR). Aircraft find targets in a specified area and coordinate the attacks of other flights on them.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the counterland control task is for, as free text.

operating_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the aircraft are on station in the area.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the counterland control task sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the counterland control task, as free text.

CounterlandControl.title: Counterland control task

CustomBrief.description: A custom brief is a set of values with names for a custom task, with the namespace of the application that gives the values.

data.description: This field contains the data of the brief, as values with names.

namespace.description: This field gives the namespace of the application or standard that gives the data, such as `org.example.task`, as free text.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates the data.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the custom task.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the custom task occurs.

assigned_actions.description: This list contains the steps of the custom task, in order. The flights do the steps in their sequence.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this custom task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

coordination.description: This field gives the coordination for the custom task, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a tasking for a custom task.

name.description: This field gives the name of this custom task, for display.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the custom task is for, as free text.

operating_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the custom task occurs.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the custom task sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

required_capabilities.description: This list contains the functions that are necessary for the flights of the custom task.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the custom task, as free text.

DocumentRef.description: A document reference is a document that a record refers to. Consumers do not get the document automatically through a network.

ElectromagneticBrief.description: An electromagnetic brief is the data for an electromagnetic attack mission.

emitters.description: This list contains the threat emitters for the electromagnetic attack, in order of priority.

orbit.description: This field identifies the orbit or zone that is the station of the aircraft during the electromagnetic attack.

protected_channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that stay clear of the electromagnetic attack.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the electromagnetic task.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the electromagnetic task occurs.

assigned_effect.description: This field gives the electromagnetic effect that the flights give, as free text. An example is `Stand-off jamming of the SA-6 radars`.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this electromagnetic task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

coordination_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that coordinates the electromagnetic task.

equipment_requirements.description: This list contains the equipment that is necessary for the electromagnetic task.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an electromagnetic tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the electromagnetic task is for, as free text.

operating_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the electromagnetic task occurs.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the electromagnetic task sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the limits and conditions that are applicable to this electromagnetic task.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the electromagnetic task, as free text.

supported_missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the electromagnetic task helps.

EmitterTarget.description: An emitter target is an emitter that is a target of the mission, with its priority.

emitter.description: This field identifies the emitter that is a target of the mission.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of this emitter. Priority 1 is the highest.

target.description: This field identifies the target that contains the emitter, when the resource catalogue has a target record for it.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the escort.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this escort. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an escort tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the escort is for, as free text.

protection_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the escort gives protection to the missions.

release_condition.description: This field gives the condition at which the escort stops the protection of the missions, as free text.

rendezvous.description: This field identifies the control point that is the rendezvous point of the escort and the missions that it gives protection to.

rendezvous_time.description: This field gives the time condition for the rendezvous of the escort. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the escort sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

separation_instructions.description: This field gives the position of the escort in relation to the missions that it gives protection to, as free text.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the escort, as free text.

supported_missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the escort helps.

FACABrief.description: A forward air controller brief is the data that the aircraft get before an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission.

cas_missions.description: This list identifies the close air support (CAS) missions that the airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) can control.

contact_points.description: This list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role `control`.

controllers.description: This list contains the agencies that control the close air support (CAS) for this airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission, with their radio channels.

fire_support_measures.description: This list identifies the fire support coordination measures and airspace coordination areas that are applicable to the airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission.

friendly_lines.description: This list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.

ground_scheme_summary.description: This field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.

holding_altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) mission.

marks.description: This list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.

x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies a mark from artillery, mortar or naval gun fire.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_pointer: This value identifies a mark from an infrared pointer. Aircrew with night vision devices can see it on the target.
x-enum-descriptions.laser: This value identifies a mark from a laser target designator.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies a mark from smoke ammunition at or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.talk_on: This value identifies a talk-on, in which the controller tells the aircrew how to find the target by voice.
x-enum-descriptions.tracer: This value identifies a mark from tracer ammunition.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

supported_unit.description: This field gives the name of the ground unit that the airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) supports, as free text.

terminal_control.description: This list contains the types of terminal attack control that the airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) can give.

aimpoints.description: This list identifies the aimpoint entries that this selection names on the fixed target.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a selection of a fixed target. The value is `fixed`.

target.description: This field identifies the fixed target that this selection names.

activities.description: This list contains the operations of this flight in the plan, such as transit, hold, station, refuelling and recovery.

aircraft_type.description: This field identifies the aircraft type that the aircraft of this flight have.

alternate_routes.description: This list identifies the routes that this flight may use as an alternative to its route.

callsign.description: This field gives the radio call sign of this flight, such as `Viper 1`, as free text.

communications.description: This list contains the radio assignments of this flight.

configuration.description: This field gives the store configuration of the aircraft in this flight, as the plan gives it.

count.description: This field gives the number of aircraft in this flight.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

fuel.description: This field gives the fuel plan of this flight.

id.description: This field identifies this flight. Other records and orders use it to refer to this flight.

identification.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) codes of this flight. It also gives the values of the data link and the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of the flight.

launch.description: This field gives the launch of this flight: a scheduled launch, an alert launch or a start in the air.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this flight, as free text.

participation.description: This field gives the control of the aircraft in this flight: pilots, the simulator or the two, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.ai: The simulator flies all aircraft of the flight.
x-enum-descriptions.mixed: Pilots and the simulator fly the aircraft of the flight.
x-enum-descriptions.player: Pilots fly all aircraft of the flight.

recovery.description: This field gives the recovery plan of this flight after the mission.

route.description: This field identifies the route that this flight follows.

spins_paragraphs.description: This list identifies the special instructions (SPINS) blocks that are applicable to this flight.

unit.description: This field gives the unit that supplies this flight, such as `Blue fighter squadron`, as free text.

flight.description: This field identifies the flight that this selection gets aircraft from.

members.description: This list contains the position numbers of the selected aircraft in the flight. Without this field, the selection contains all aircraft of the flight.

bingo.description: This field gives the bingo fuel, which is the fuel quantity at which the flight starts to go back to base.

initial.description: This field gives the fuel at the start of the mission. The value is a quantity with its unit, or a percentage of full fuel in the aircraft and in the external tanks.

joker.description: This field gives the joker fuel, which is a fuel quantity more than the bingo fuel. At the joker fuel, the flight changes its plan.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this fuel plan, as free text.

reserve.description: This field gives the fuel that the flight keeps as a reserve at landing.

GeoPoint.description: A geographic point is a position in WGS 84 decimal degrees. An adapter is necessary for the Cartesian coordinates of a simulator.

datalink_network.description: This field gives the name of the data link network of this flight, as free text.

datalink_station.description: This field gives the station number of this flight in the data link, as free text.

datalink_type.description: This field gives the type of data link, such as `Link 16`, as free text.

instructions.description: This list contains the instructions for identification.

mode_1.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode 1 code, as two digits from 0 to 7.

mode_2.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode 2 code, as four digits from 0 to 7.

mode_3.description: This field gives the identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode 3 code, as four digits from 0 to 7.

mode_4.description: This field gives the condition of identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode 4, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.as_directed: The flight sets the mode as the instructions of the mission tell it.
x-enum-descriptions.off: The identification, friend or foe (IFF) transponder does not operate in Mode 4.
x-enum-descriptions.on: The identification, friend or foe (IFF) transponder operates in Mode 4.

mode_5.description: This field gives the condition of identification, friend or foe (IFF) mode 5, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.as_directed: The flight sets the mode as the instructions of the mission tell it.
x-enum-descriptions.off: The identification, friend or foe (IFF) transponder does not operate in Mode 5.
x-enum-descriptions.on: The identification, friend or foe (IFF) transponder operates in Mode 5.

tacan.description: This field gives the channel, band and identifier of the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of this flight, for air-to-air operation.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a time condition in a window.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the event occurs.

external_percent.description: This field gives the fuel in the external tanks, as a part of their full fuel, in percent.

internal_percent.description: This field gives the fuel in the tanks in the aircraft, as a part of their full fuel, in percent.

cargo.description: This list contains the cargo items of the transport mission.

passengers.description: This field gives the number of persons on the aircraft of the transport mission.

personnel_notes.description: This field gives the notes about the personnel on the aircraft of the transport mission, as free text.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the fuel quantity, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.lb: The mass is in pounds. One pound is 0.45359237 kilograms.

value.description: This field gives the fuel quantity as a number, in the unit that `unit` gives.

Mission.description: A mission is a task that the order gives, with a mission number, one typed tasking and the flights for it. The consumer keeps the condition of the allocation and of the execution.

constraints.description: This list contains the limits that are applicable to this mission.

contingencies.description: This list contains the steps in the plan for conditions that change the plan of this mission.

control.description: This field gives the control of this mission: a command and control agency, or one of the flights of the mission.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

flights.description: This list contains the flights that the order gives to the mission. When the list is empty, the tasking has no allocation.

id.description: This field identifies this mission. Other records and orders use it to refer to this mission.

mission_number.description: This field identifies this mission. Each mission in the order has a different identifier. Units use the mission number to refer to the mission on kneeboards and by voice.

package.description: This field identifies the package that contains this mission.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of this mission in the order. Priority 1 is the highest.

request_refs.description: This list contains the references to the requests that this mission is for.

support.description: This list contains the flights that help this mission, with their roles.

tasking.description: This field gives the one typed tasking of this mission.

tasking_relationship.description: This field gives the relation between the order and this mission, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.coordination_only: The order shows the mission only for coordination, and does not task it.

threat_refs.description: This list identifies the possible threats that are applicable to this mission.

Mission.title: Mission

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a selected mobile target.

target.description: This field identifies the mobile target that this selection contains.

Offset.description: An offset is a number of minutes from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it. The value can be less than zero.

OnCallCAS.description: An on-call close air support (CAS) tasking is a tasking for the on-call type of preplanned close air support, or for immediate close air support. JP 3-09.3 (2014) paragraph 27 gives these types. On-call aircraft wait on ground alert or airborne alert until they get a request. Immediate close air support is for requests that are not in the plan.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the on-call close air support (CAS).

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the on-call close air support (CAS) operates.

availability.description: This field gives the time interval during which the on-call close air support (CAS) is available.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this on-call close air support (CAS) tasking. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

check_in_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flights follow at the start of the on-call close air support (CAS).

kind.description: The value identifies this record as an on-call close air support (CAS) tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the on-call close air support (CAS) is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the on-call close air support (CAS) sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

request_refs.description: This list contains the references to the air support requests that this tasking is for.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the on-call close air support (CAS), as free text.

supported_force.description: This field gives the ground force that the on-call close air support (CAS) helps, as free text.

target_assignment_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives targets to the on-call close air support (CAS) flights.

tasking_agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that tasks the on-call close air support (CAS) flights.

terminal_control.description: This field gives the type of terminal attack control for the on-call close air support (CAS), as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.assigned_by_controller: The controller sets the type for each attack.
x-enum-descriptions.type_1: This value identifies terminal attack control of type 1. The controller sees the attack aircraft and the target, and gives clearance for each attack.
x-enum-descriptions.type_2: This value identifies terminal attack control of type 2. The controller gives clearance for each attack, but cannot see the attack aircraft or the target when the aircraft releases the weapon.
x-enum-descriptions.type_3: This value identifies terminal attack control of type 3. The controller gives one clearance for more than one attack in one engagement, with attack restrictions.

OnCallCAS.title: OnCallCAS

authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives the order for the event.

condition.description: This field gives the condition in which the authority gives the order for the event, as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a time condition on order.

commander.description: This field identifies the flight and the aircraft of the package commander.

coordination.description: This list contains the coordination instructions for the missions of the package.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this package. Other records and orders use it to refer to this package.

name.description: This field gives the name of this package, for display.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the package is for, as free text.

rendezvous.description: This field identifies the control point that is the rendezvous point of the package.

rendezvous_time.description: This field gives the time condition for the rendezvous of the package. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the combat air patrol (CAP).

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the patrol, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure that contains the combat air patrol (CAP) station.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this combat air patrol (CAP). The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

coverage_responsibility.description: This field gives the air threats and airspace that are the task of the combat air patrol (CAP), as free text.

engagement_instructions.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the commit criteria and the engagement conditions of the combat air patrol (CAP).

handover.description: This field gives the instructions for the handover of the combat air patrol (CAP) station to the subsequent flight, as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a combat air patrol (CAP) tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the combat air patrol (CAP) is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the combat air patrol (CAP) sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

station_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the combat air patrol (CAP) flights are on station.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the combat air patrol (CAP), as free text.

Period.description: A period is a time interval between two absolute date-times in the RFC 3339 format.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the personnel recovery.

availability.description: This field gives the time interval during which the personnel recovery asset is available.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this personnel recovery task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

coordination_agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that coordinates the personnel recovery.

incident.description: This field gives the event that isolates the personnel, as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a personnel recovery tasking.

medical_requirements.description: This field gives the medical treatment that is necessary for the isolated personnel, as free text.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the personnel recovery is for, as free text.

recognition_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that lets the recovery force and the isolated personnel identify each other.

recovery_destination.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that receives the personnel after the recovery.

recovery_method.description: This field gives the method that the aircraft use for the recovery, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.assigned_on_scene: The commander at the site of the recovery sets the method.
x-enum-descriptions.hoist: The aircraft stays in the air and lifts the personnel into it.
x-enum-descriptions.land: The aircraft lands to get the personnel.
x-enum-descriptions.pickup: This value identifies a pickup of the personnel from the surface.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the personnel recovery sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

role.description: This field gives the role of the personnel recovery: search and rescue (SAR) or combat search and rescue (CSAR), as one of the enumerated values. The role is different from the recovery method. The role does not make a control measure.

x-enum-descriptions.combat_search_and_rescue: This value identifies combat search and rescue (CSAR), which is the recovery of isolated personnel during combat.
x-enum-descriptions.search_and_rescue: This value identifies search and rescue (SAR), which is aid to persons in distress in a permissive environment.

search_area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the recovery force does a search for the isolated personnel.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the personnel recovery, as free text.

tasking_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that tasks the recovery force.

PersonnelRecoveryBrief.description: A personnel recovery brief is the data that a recovery aircrew gets before the mission. The brief identifies the isolated personnel report (ISOPREP) of a survivor and contains no other data about the person.

egress_route.description: This field identifies the route that the recovery flights use after the recovery.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the recovery flights use to hold.

ingress_route.description: This field identifies the route that the recovery flights use to fly to the objective area.

on_scene_commander.description: This field identifies the flight that is the on-scene commander.

pickup_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the recovery flights plan to be at the survivors.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

rescort_missions.description: This list identifies the rescue escort (RESCORT) missions that defend the recovery.

survivors.description: This list contains the isolated persons for this recovery.

PinnedRef.description: A pinned reference is a dependency on a local document that consumers examine by identifier and revision.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the preplanned attack.

assignments.description: This list contains the attack assignments of the preplanned attack. Each assignment gives one target to one or more selected aircraft.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this preplanned attack. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a preplanned attack tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the preplanned attack is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the preplanned attack sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

role.description: This field gives the attack role of this preplanned attack, as one of the enumerated values. The value `scheduled_cas` is for close air support (CAS) at a scheduled time. On-call CAS and immediate close air support use the tasking for on-call CAS.

x-enum-descriptions.air_interdiction: This value identifies air interdiction, which is an attack on enemy surface forces before they can engage friendly forces. The attack occurs at a distance from friendly forces.
x-enum-descriptions.dead: This value identifies an attack that destroys enemy air defences on the surface. After the attack, they cannot engage aircraft again. This is an openAIX value with no doctrinal source.
x-enum-descriptions.maritime_attack: This value identifies an attack on maritime surface targets.
x-enum-descriptions.scheduled_cas: This value identifies preplanned close air support (CAS) at a time on target that the schedule gives. JP 3-09.3 (2014) paragraph 27 gives this type of CAS.
x-enum-descriptions.sead: This value identifies an attack that neutralizes or temporarily degrades enemy air defences on the surface, or destroys them.
x-enum-descriptions.strike: This value identifies an attack on surface targets in the plan.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the preplanned attack, as free text.

supporting_request.description: This field gives a reference to the air support request that the preplanned attack is for.

action.description: This field gives the task of this step, as free text.

completion.description: This field gives the condition at which this step is completed, as free text.

condition.description: This field gives the condition in which this step is applicable, as free text.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that this assignment uses.

preset.description: This field gives the preset number of the radio channel on the radio of the aircraft.

purpose.description: This field gives the operation or objective of this radio assignment, as free text.

radio.description: This field gives the radio of the aircraft that uses the channel, such as `UHF` or `VHF`, as free text.

flight.description: This field identifies the receiver flight that this entry gives a refuelling window to.

planned_offload.description: This field gives the fuel that the tanker plans to give to the receiver flight in this window.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the receiver flight gets fuel from the tanker.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the reconnaissance.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this reconnaissance task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a reconnaissance tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the reconnaissance is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the reconnaissance sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

reporting_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flights follow to send the information.

requirements.description: This list contains the collection entries of the reconnaissance.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the reconnaissance, as free text.

ReconnaissanceBrief.description: A reconnaissance brief is the data for a reconnaissance mission. The collection entries of the tasking give the information, the sensors and the times.

named_areas.description: This list identifies the named areas of interest, target areas of interest or reconnaissance areas that the aircraft look at.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

reporting.description: This field gives the reports of the reconnaissance aircraft, with the method and the time.

alternates.description: This list identifies the alternative operating locations that the flight may use for recovery. An operating location is an airfield, a carrier or a forward arming and refuelling point (FARP).

destination.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that the flight goes back to.

planned_time.description: This field gives the time of the recovery, as the plan gives it. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flight follows for recovery.

restrictions.description: This list contains the limits and conditions that are applicable to this recovery.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the refuelling task.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the refuelling task, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure that contains the refuelling track or anchor.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this refuelling task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that connects the tanker and the receivers.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a refuelling tasking.

method.description: This field gives the refuelling systems that the tanker supplies for this tasking: `boom`, `drogue` (probe and drogue) or `both`, as one of the enumerated values.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the refuelling task is for, as free text.

planned_offload.description: This field gives the total fuel that the tanker plans to give on this tasking.

receivers.description: This list contains the receiver flights in the schedule of the tanker, with their windows and the fuel that the tanker plans to give.

rendezvous_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the receivers follow to go to the tanker.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the refuelling task sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

station_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the tanker is on station.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the refuelling task, as free text.

tacan.description: This field gives the channel, band and identifier of the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of the tanker for this tasking, in air-to-air mode.

unassigned_receiver_policy.description: This field gives the instruction for receivers that have no window in the schedule of the tanker, as free text.

RefuelingBrief.description: A refuelling brief is the data that tanker and receiver aircrews get before the refuelling. The tasking gives the track, the altitude block, the refuelling method, the channel, the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) and the receivers.

anchor.description: This field identifies the orbit, point or air-to-air refuelling area that is the anchor of the refuelling track.

control_time.description: This field gives the time at which the tanker and the first receiver are at the rendezvous point.

receiver_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude at which the receivers join the tanker, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

rendezvous.description: This field gives the type of rendezvous between the tanker and the receivers, as one of the enumerated values. The values are openAIX values with no doctrinal source.

rendezvous_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the rendezvous point of the tanker and the receivers.

ReportingPlan.description: A report plan is the reports that an aircrew sends, with the method and the time of the reports.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that is for the reports.

deadline.description: This field gives the time before which the aircrew sends the reports.

method.description: This field gives the method that the aircrew uses to send the reports, as one of the enumerated values.

recipient.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the reports.

reports.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports.

SCARBrief.description: A strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR) brief is the data for a SCAR mission.

attack_missions.description: This list identifies the attack missions that the strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR) aircraft coordinate.

controller.description: This field gives the agency that controls the sequence of the attack flights, with its radio channels.

entry_points.description: This list identifies the points that the attack flights fly through when they go into the area. Each point shall have the role `control` or `ingress` or `gate`.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the attack flights use to hold.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

reporting.description: This field gives the reports of the strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR) aircraft, with the method and the time.

stack.description: This list contains the altitude blocks of the holding stack, each for one attack mission.

altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of this level of the stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

mission.description: This field identifies the attack mission that holds at this level of the stack.

target_priorities.description: This list contains the types of target that the strike coordination and reconnaissance (SCAR) aircraft look for, with their priorities.

category.description: This field gives the type of target, as one of the enumerated values. The values are openAIX values with no doctrinal source.

priority.description: This field gives the priority of the type of target. Priority 1 is the highest.

authority.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives approval for the standard conventional load (SCL) of this alternative.

condition.description: This field gives the condition in which the flight uses the standard conventional load (SCL) of this alternative, as free text.

scl.description: This field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) of this alternative.

SEADBrief.description: A suppression of enemy air defences (SEAD) brief is the emitters for the suppression, the employment procedure and the missions that the suppression helps.

emitters.description: This list contains the threat emitters for the suppression, in order of priority.

employment_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the employment and the rules of engagement (ROE) of the anti-radiation missiles.

protected_missions.description: This list identifies the missions that the suppression helps.

suppression_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the suppression of the threat emitters occurs.

departure.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that the flight starts its mission from.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a scheduled launch.

startup.description: This field gives the time at which the flight starts the engines of its aircraft. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

takeoff.description: This field gives the time at which the flight does the take-off. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

taxi.description: This field gives the time at which the flight starts to taxi. The value is a date and time, or an offset in minutes from the start of the order period.

instructions.description: This field gives the instructions for self control, as free text.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as self control.

responsible_flight.description: This field identifies the flight that controls the mission.

Speed.description: A speed is a speed with its unit: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the speed: knots, kilometres in one hour or Mach number, as one of the enumerated values. The suffix `_ias` identifies an indicated airspeed (IAS), and the suffix `_tas` identifies a true airspeed (TAS).

value.description: This field gives the value of the speed, in the unit of `unit`.

Speed.title: Speed

coordination.description: This field gives the coordination between this mission and the flight that helps it, as free text.

flight.description: This field identifies the flight that helps this mission.

role.description: This field gives the role of the flight that helps this mission, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.airborne_control: This value identifies an aircraft, such as an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft, that gives surveillance and control to the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.controller: This value identifies a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) that gives terminal attack control to the mission.
